rubric_scores.justification: The output correctly identifies PAN-at-rest in the Card-Data Vault (RDS) as the crown jewel ('PAN at rest, KMS', 'Tokenization Service is your crown-jewel single point of compromise', 'highest-value asset') and gives a concrete attack path ('KMS key compromise or over-broad key policy -> bulk PAN decryption'). It ties to least-privilege KMS and field-level encryption. However it does NOT classify PAN as RESTRICTED, does NOT use an OWASP Risk score (17-25 / Impact 5), and does NOT rank a single PAN-bulk-exfiltration finding as #1. The P0 list ranks 'Plaintext PAN in transit between internal services' as #1, with the Tokenization/KMS crown-jewel finding only at P0 #3. Per R1 the #1 must be the PAN-exfil OR the lateral-movement-to-vault finding; #1 here is the in-transit tampering finding, which is MF3/R3, not R1/R2. Crown-jewel identification and attack path are solid (would be pass), but the missing RESTRICTED classification, missing OWASP score band, and the #1-ranking miss drop this to partial.

Strongly covered. The output flags the no-mTLS / unauthenticated east-west traffic as a P0 finding (#2 'Flat trust model — no internal authentication/authorization (JWT not re-validated on internal hops, no mTLS, single VPC)'). It covers BOTH Spoofing ('No mTLS -> any workload ... can impersonate the Payments Service and call the Tokenization Service directly') and Lateral Movement ('Lateral movement: foothold in Fraud-Scoring or Analytics -> reach Tokenization/vault because internal calls are unauthenticated'), explicitly invokes zero-trust ('zero-trust internal posture — per-service identity', 'adopt a zero-trust internal model') and 'network position != trust' in spirit (' "trusted network" is not a justification'), with a concrete pivot path from a compromised ECS task/pod to the Tokenization Service/Vault. Severity is P0/critical, well above HIGH. Meets all R2 elements.

Cardholder-data-in-transit tampering on internal plaintext hops is flagged at P0 (#1 'Plaintext PAN in transit between internal services'), with Tampering called out explicitly ('Plaintext HTTP/gRPC inside VPC -> on-path tampering of card data / token responses') and Information Disclosure ('PAN traverses the network unencrypted between services. Packet capture, VPC traffic mirroring...'). It cites 'PCI 4.0 req 4.x' for transit and separately ties stored-PAN to 'PCI 4.0 4.2.1' and KMS/at-rest protections; PCI-DSS scope is acknowledged throughout (CDE scoping section, '6.4.3', '11.6.1', '8.4.2/8.5', '10.x'). Although it references PCI v4.0 numbering rather than 'Req 3'/'Req 4' verbatim, it explicitly maps transit encryption to PCI req 4.x and at-rest protection to PCI crypto reqs, satisfying the criterion's substance.

Both halves covered. Analytics pipeline: 'PAN/PII sprawl into S3/Redshift. Public S3 bucket, over-broad Redshift access ... If any PAN reaches here, Redshift/S3/BI users all become CDE ... classic scope-explosion finding' (P1 #4), explicitly naming CDE scope expansion, unmasked-PAN replication, and object-storage misconfiguration. Third-party fraud API: 'What cardholder/PII data is sent to the third party?', 'MITM on egress alters fraud verdict', 'Compromised egress path used for data exfil', and availability dependency 'Third-party outage/timeout stalls or fails-open transactions' (P1 #7). It covers data leakage, egress/exfil, and availability. (It does not name SSRF/CWE-918 or OWASP API10 explicitly, but R4 lists these as alternatives 'and/or' and the substantive risks are surfaced.)

Admin Console privileged functions flagged as Elevation: 'Refund manipulation (issue fraudulent refunds), merchant config tampering (re-route settlements)' and Elevation row 'Broad admin role ... IDOR letting one ops user act on another merchant', with recommendations for 'least-privilege RBAC, per-merchant authorization checks'. The cross-cutting JWT section explicitly flags 'No internal JWT re-validation -> a token (or no token at all) is sufficient once past the gateway' and recommends 'Re-validate and enforce authorization at each sensitive service, especially Tokenization and refund endpoints.' P1 #6 calls for MFA, unique accounts, RBAC, refund approval/limits. This is broken function-level authorization plus step-up/internal authZ. (OWASP API5/A01 not cited by ID, but the substance — BFLA and not relying solely on gateway JWT — is fully present.)

The criterion requires all four DFD layers as VALID MERMAID (L1 Architecture, L2 Trust & Identity, L3 Data with [ENC]/[PLAIN] edge labels, L4 Threat Overlay with risk coloring and an attack-path overlay reaching the vault, marking Vault/Tokenization highRisk). The output provides only ASCII/text DFDs in code fences, not Mermaid. There is no L1/L2/L3/L4 layered taxonomy, no [ENC]/[PLAIN] edge annotations (it uses prose like 'NO mTLS, plaintext channel'), no Mermaid graph syntax, and no highRisk node styling/risk coloring. Section header is literally 'Data Flow Diagrams (textual)'. None of the four required Mermaid layers are delivered.

The criterion requires STRIDE-LM with OWASP Risk Rating (Likelihood x Impact, 1-5 each) and correct severity bands, plus valid MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs and CWE IDs from the reference set (e.g., T1078, T1021, T1530, CWE-311/312/862/918), with no fabricated IDs. The output uses STRIDE per component but does NOT include the 'LM' category as a STRIDE-LM dimension in its tables (lateral movement appears under Elevation/Spoofing rows). There is no OWASP Likelihood x Impact 1-5 scoring — severity is expressed as ad hoc P0-P3 bands. No MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs and no CWE IDs appear anywhere. The quantitative scoring and framework-ID requirements are entirely absent.

The required report template is not delivered. Missing: Executive Summary with posture rating + finding counts (no exec summary at all); Asset Inventory (assets discussed in prose but no inventory section); Threat Actor Profiles (no Organized Crime/payment-fraud or Malicious Insider profiles anywhere); Findings in TM-NNN format (findings are 'P0 #1', 'P1 #4', etc., not TM-NNN); Remediation Roadmap with waves/quick wins (there is a 'Top Recommendations' list but no waved roadmap). Architecture and Risk Overlay 'diagrams' are textual, not the template's diagram sections. Assumptions/Scope section and per-finding remediations ARE present ('Fix:' on each prioritized item), but the bulk of the mandated template structure is absent, so this fails.

summary: The output is a genuine, substantively strong threat model that surfaces every one of the six must-find threats with the right asset, the right risk category, severity at or above the required minimum, and plausible attack paths: PAN-at-rest crown jewel with KMS-decrypt bulk-exfil path (MF1, P0/critical), no-mTLS unauthenticated east-west enabling spoofing + lateral movement to the vault with explicit zero-trust framing (MF2, P0), plaintext PAN-in-transit tampering/interception tied to PCI req 4 (MF3, P0/#1), Admin Console refund/config EoP plus internal-authZ gap (MF4, P1), analytics-pipeline CDE scope explosion into S3/Redshift (MF5, P1), and third-party fraud-API data-leakage/egress/availability risk (MF6, P1). Content quality on the security substance (R2-R5) is excellent. The decisive weaknesses are structural and format-driven: it ignores the skill's prescribed deliverable shape. DFDs are textual ASCII rather than the four required Mermaid layers with [ENC]/[PLAIN] edges and highRisk overlay (R6 fail); there is no OWASP Likelihood x Impact scoring, no STRIDE-LM 'LM' column, and zero MITRE ATT&CK or CWE IDs (R7 fail); and the mandated report template — Executive Summary with posture/counts, Asset Inventory, Threat Actor Profiles, TM-NNN findings, waved Remediation Roadmap, Networking section — is largely absent (R8 fail). R1 is partial because PAN is not classified RESTRICTED, no OWASP score band is applied, and the #1-ranked finding is the in-transit (MF3) rather than the PAN-exfil/lateral-movement finding R1 demands. Weighted, the three full fails on heavily weighted format/framework items (R6=4, R7=3, R8=3) plus partial R1 (5) put the score well below the 0.8 pass threshold despite full must-find coverage."
